Answer: B
Reason: Extralobar pulmonary sequestrations typically present as well-defined, homogeneous masses in the lower thorax (often left-sided) that are separate from the normal lung parenchyma and frequently exhibit a distinct pleuro-vertebral interface or paravertebral location due to their own visceral pleura. Option B accurately describes these characteristic radiographic features (well-defined margin, paravertebral position, distinct interface) that distinguish it from intralobar sequestration or other mediastinal masses.
